text: You have honed your senses and gained increased reflexes.
You add your level to your Notice Bonus
You gain a +1d4 Skill Bonus on Notice Checks, a +1 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +4 to Skill Bonus Higher Notice.
You gain a +2d4 Skill Bonus on Notice Checks, a +2 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +8 to Skill Bonus Higher Notice.
You gain a +3d4 Skill Bonus on Notice Checks, a +3 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +12 to Skill Bonus Higher Notice.
Whenever you gain a rank in the ~\nameref{perk:increase{{value}}} Perk, you gain 1d8 instead of 1d6.
Don't re-roll previous ranks of the pool value.
Instead, you gain 1 point for each rank you already have for that pool value.
You gain 1d10 instead of 1d12
You gain 1 point for each existing rank
You gain 1d12 instead of 1d10
You gain 1 point for each existing rank
You increase one of your Attribute values by one.

If you increase Strength, Intellect, Vitality, or Charisma, then your Stamina, Mana, Health, or Faith respectively also increase by 1, plus 1 for each rank of ~
ameref{perk:increaseStamina},~
ameref{perk:increaseMana},~
ameref{perk:increaseHealth}, or ~
ameref{perk:increaseFaith} you have.
Each time you gain a higher rank for this perk, you increase an Attribute value by one point.
You increase your Maximum (and current) {{value}} by 1D6 + {{param1}}.
Each time you gain a higher Rank for this perk, your {{value}} is increased again.
You are able to communicate in a specific language.
This includes reading, writing, understanding and speaking said language.
The difficulty of a language is based on the family that this language belongs to.

The LP costs of learning a new language of the same family or alphabet is reduced by 25 \% if it is the second language in the same family or alphabet that a character learns, and by 50\% for the third and further languages.
You have become agile and can move around more.
You add your level to Agility when determining Movement distance.
You gain a +2 Skill Bonus to Agility when determining Movement distance.
You gain a +4 Skill Bonus to Agility when determining Movement distance.
You gain a +8 Skill Bonus to Agility when determining Movement distance.
You have become strong-willed and aren't as easily swayed anymore.
You add your level to your Willpower bonus
You gain a +1d4 Skill Bonus on Willpower Checks, a +1 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +4 to Skill Bonus Higher Willpower.
You gain a +2d4 Skill Bonus on Willpower Checks, a +2 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +8 to Skill Bonus Higher Willpower.
You gain a +3d4 Skill Bonus on Willpower Checks, a +3 Skill Bonus to Lower, and a +12 to Skill Bonus Higher Willpower.
You are trained with all weapons that have the "Simple" descriptor.
You add your level to attack and block rolls made with that weapon.
You also gain a +{{oldRank}}d4 Skill Bonus to attack and block rolls with these weapons.
This is a set of different perks.
You are trained with a certain type of weapon that has the "Unusual" descriptor.
You add your level to attack and block rolls made with that weapon.
You choose the weapon type that you are proficient in when you choose this perk.
You can gain another instance of this perk by choosing a different weapon.
You also gain a +{{oldRank}}d4 Skill Bonus to attack and block rolls with these weapons.
You are trained with {{value}} weapons.
This includes all weapons with the "{{value}}" and without the "Unusual" descriptor.
You add your level to attack and block rolls made with these weapons.
you gain a +{{oldRank}}d4 attack and block rolls made with these weapons
This is a set of different perks.
You are trained with one type of weapon (Like "Arming Sword" or "Light Crossbow") that does not have the "Unusual" descriptor.
You add your level to attack and block rolls made with that weapon.
You choose the weapon type that you are proficient in when you choose this perk.
You can gain another instance of this perk by choosing a different weapon.
You also gain a +{{oldRank}}d4 Skill Bonus to attack and block rolls with these weapons.
You can spend 2 additional AP to create an opening in your opponent's defenses, to be able to hit easier.
When making a melee weapon attack, make a Charisma check adding bonuses for deception, contested by the defender's Notice.
If your roll is above the defender's maximum Notice, the target can not react to your attack.
If the defender makes a Notice check and succeeds, their Dodge (as well as Maximum and Minimum Dodge) suffers a Distraction Malus equals to your Deception Roll minus their Minimum Notice.
If your Deception roll is below their minimum Notice, the target can react normally.

When making a melee weapon attack based on Strength, you can pay 4 Stamina and suffer a Skill Malus to that Attack of up to -2, while gaining a Skill Bonus to Weapon Damage equal to the same amount, but positive.
For example, if your weapon would deal 2D4 damage, and you had 8 Strength, you could pay 4 Stamina and Suffer a Skill Malus to the attack roll of -2, changing the weapon's damage to 2d4+2.
When using this weapon with a two-handed weapon attack, the Skill Damage bonus is doubled.
Requires {{conditionalText[0]}} Strength
{{conditionalText[1]}} Stamina for up to {{conditionalText[0]}} points.
When making a weapon attack based on Agility, you can pay up to 4 Stamina and gain a Skill Bonus to Weapon Damage equal to half that number.
This Bonus is doubled for unarmed strikes.
Requires {{conditionalText[0]}} Agility
You now pay up to {{conditionalText[1]}} Stamina to increase the Weapon damage by half that number.

When making a melee weapon attack with a weapon you are proficient with, if that attack deals at least 1 damage, you can spend 10 Stamina to make an additional trip attempt (You don't have to pay the usual Stamina for that attempt).\
When making a weapon attack based on Dexterity, you can increase the AP cost of the attack by up to 2.
If you do so, you gain a Skill Bonus to attack and damage for that attack equal to that value.
If the attack is ranged, this Bonus is doubled.
Requires {{conditionalText[0]}} Dexterity
You can use increase the attack's cost by up to {{conditionalText[0]}} AP

When you hit a creature with a weapon attack based on DEX or AGI, and the creature cannot react (for example, if they're not aware of you, or if the attack roll was above their maximum dodge), you can spend 3 additional Stamina.
If you do so, you gain an additional +1d6 Skill Bonus to the damage of the attack, and you bypass any damage reduction the target gains from armor.
Enemies immune to critical hits are immune to this effect.
Skill Bonus is now +{{newRank}}d6 damage.
You can run towards an enemy and attack them with a melee weapon attack.
To do so, you spend 5 additional Stamina, and you only spend the AP of the Run or the Attack Action, whichever is higher.
For example, if the run costs 5 AP, and the Attack costs 6 AP, you spend 6 AP instead of 11, in addition to 13 Stamina.
When making a melee weapon attack that deals at least 1 damage, you can spend 10 Stamina to gain a free disarm attempt without having to attack again or pay any additional AP or Stamina.
While having either a Weapon or Shield drawn in this style, you gain a +2 Attention bonus to Dodge and Notice.
Requires {{conditionalText[0]}} agility.
The bonus is now +{{conditionalText[1]}} Attention bonus.

Elves are a species of tall-standing, fair skinned creatures that have adapted to different environments through magical means.
Elves mature at an age of 50, and can live up to 500 years - there is however no known case of an Elf dying of old age.
At their best, Elves are reliable, honest and knowledgeable.
At their worst, Elves are hard-headed, aloof and emotionless.
Elves cannot be put to sleep, and don't require sleep in general.
Instead, they simply have to meditate for 4 hours per day.
While doing so, they suffer a -6 concentration malus to perception
As an Elf, you are part of one of three subspecies
High Elves live in cities of art and splendor, and love magic and poetry.
Woodland Elves are excellent hunters, climbers, and can swing from tree to tree without effort.

Gnomes are a very short species of empathic people that have a deep bond with nature.
Gnomes mature at the age of 40, and can live to the age of 350.
At their best, gnomes are friendly, calm and wise.
At their worst, gnomes are stubborn, close-minded and vengeful.
Gnomes have a supernatural gift that allows them to understand and talk to animals as if they were speaking their language.
In most situations however, animals have a very short memory and aren't intelligent enough for deep conversation.
